skill.name: reading-logseq-data
skill.description: Read Logseq graph data through the local HTTP API or Logseq CLI. The skill helps fetch pages, blocks, backlinks, properties, search results, and Datalog query results.
skill.summary: Read Logseq pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, and Datalog query results from a local graph.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The skill performs legitimate read-only Logseq operations, but it includes real network access, environment token handling, and CLI execution. Most documentation and Datalog template findings are false positives, while the CLI query path, token handling, and query interpolation deserve remediation before broad publication.

remediation.issue: User-controlled search text is interpolated into a Datalog query.
remediation.suggestion: Use Datalog parameters or strict escaping for search text before executing fallback queries.

remediation.issue: The CLI backend can pass an API token in command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Avoid placing tokens in argv; use a secure config file, stdin, or another mechanism not visible in process listings.

remediation.issue: Authenticated HTTP requests can use a configurable API URL.
remediation.suggestion: Default to loopback and warn or require confirmation before sending bearer tokens to non-loopback endpoints.

remediation.issue: The skill executes the local Logseq CLI for query operations.
remediation.suggestion: Document the external command behavior and validate query inputs before invoking the CLI backend.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Datalog Query Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: The search fallback embeds query_text directly inside a Datalog string before execution. A crafted search value could alter query syntax or broaden graph reads when the fallback path is used.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The f-string at the fallback query includes query_text directly inside the query body. The skill also supports executing that generated query through HTTP or CLI backends.

semantic_findings.title: API Token Passed Through CLI Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The CLI backend can append the API token to the command argument list before subprocess execution. Command arguments can be exposed through local process inspection or captured in logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The token is added to cmd with --in-app and -a, then the full command list is passed to subprocess.run. This is a common local secret exposure pattern even without shell injection.

content.value_statement: Logseq users need structured access to notes, tasks, links, and properties without manual browsing. This skill provides guided read operations through the local API or CLI.
actual_capabilities: Fetch Logseq pages and include child blocks when requested.
Read individual blocks by UUID and return their properties.
Run Datalog queries against a Logseq graph through HTTP or CLI backends.
Search block content and limit returned results.
List pages, page properties, block properties, and backlinks.
Load Logseq API URL, token, and graph path from environment or local config.
limitations: Requires a running Logseq HTTP API or installed Logseq CLI.
Needs a valid API token for HTTP operations.
Focused on read operations, not editing or creating Logseq content.
Custom queries can expose large portions of a graph if written broadly.

use_cases.title: Inspect research notes
use_cases.description: Fetch pages, backlinks, and related blocks for a topic before summarizing findings.

use_cases.title: Audit task metadata
use_cases.description: Query tasks by status, priority, deadline, or custom properties across a Logseq graph.

use_cases.title: Build knowledge graph reports
use_cases.description: Use Datalog patterns to extract structured page, tag, property, and relationship data.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch a page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to read the Logseq page named "Project Plan" and summarize its main blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Find backlinks
prompt_templates.prompt: Find all Logseq blocks that reference the page "Customer Research" and group them by source page.

prompt_templates.title: Search task content
prompt_templates.prompt: Search my Logseq graph for blocks that mention "release blocker" and return the top 20 results with page names.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Datalog report
prompt_templates.prompt: Write and run a Datalog query that lists open tasks with priority, deadline, and parent page, then explain the results.

output_examples.input: Read the page "Weekly Review" and include its child blocks.
output_examples.output: A page summary with the title, page properties, key child blocks, and any missing page warning.
A grouped backlink list showing each referring page, matching block text, and relationship context.

output_examples.input: List high priority tasks due before next month.
output_examples.output: A concise task report with task titles, status, due dates, and the page where each task appears.

best_practices: Use narrow Datalog pulls so results include only needed fields.
Prefer query parameters for values that come from user input.
Keep Logseq API tokens local and restrict custom API URLs to trusted endpoints.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad pull-all queries when a smaller field list is enough.
Do not paste secrets or private tokens into prompts or query text.
Do not point the API URL at an untrusted remote service.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my Logseq graph?
faq.answer: No. The documented operations focus on reading pages, blocks, properties, backlinks, search results, and query results.

faq.question: What connection methods does it support?
faq.answer: It can use the Logseq HTTP API first and fall back to the Logseq CLI when available.

faq.question: Does it require a Logseq API token?
faq.answer: HTTP operations require a token. The skill can read it from parameters, environment variables, or local configuration.

faq.question: Can it run custom Datalog queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples and templates for Datalog queries against a Logseq graph.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing it?
faq.answer: Review command execution, token handling, custom API URL behavior, and user-provided Datalog query construction.
